evidence: Hor. S. 2.1.55: ut neque calce lupus quemquam neque dente petit bōs
terms.comment: Horace’s phrase for an animal’s kick at someone, as against pede pulsāre of a ball.

phrases.latin: Baba, in sellā sedēns, pilam puerō pede impellit; puer eam pede pulsat, ut potest
phrases.english: Baba, sitting on a chair, pushes the ball to the boy with her foot; the boy kicks it as best he can

phrases.latin: ut neque calce lupus quemquam neque dente petit bōs
phrases.english: just as a wolf doesn’t kick anyone, nor an ox bite

sources: Lewis & Short: ico · Lewis & Short: calx
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, pp. 44, 47, 50, 336.
